notes: AP History Practices/Skills (1.A-6.D) are shared across AP World History, AP U.S. History, and AP European History CEDs; the skills and reasoning-process sections below are identical to the verified AP World History code list (skills verified against the AP World CED mirror and multiple mutually-corroborating CB AP Course Audit sample syllabi; skill sub-code descriptors quoted verbatim from the APUSH CED unit guides, accessed 2026-10-02). APUSH topic codes verified DIRECTLY against the official College Board AP U.S. History Course and Exam Description (Effective Fall 2019) unit guides for all 9 periods (see source_urls), with 6.14/7.15 corroborated via the pubhtml5 full-CED mirror and the official CB pacing guide. Topic titles are framework content, unchanged by the Fall 2026 CED which altered exam format only. Do NOT invent codes: any skill_code/topic_code not in this file is invalid.

reasoning_processes.description: Describe similarities and/or differences between different historical developments or processes.
reasoning_processes.name: Comparison

reasoning_processes.description: Describe the causes and/or effects of a specific historical development or process.
reasoning_processes.name: Causation

reasoning_processes.description: Describe patterns of continuity and/or change over time.
reasoning_processes.name: Continuity and Change

skills.description: Identify a historical concept, development, or process.
Explain a historical concept, development, or process.
Identify a source's point of view, purpose, historical situation, and/or audience.
Explain the point of view, purpose, historical situation, and/or audience of a source.
Explain the significance of a source's point of view, purpose, historical situation, and/or audience, including how these might limit the use(s) of a source.
Identify and describe a claim and/or argument in a text-based or non-text-based source.
Identify the evidence used in a source to support an argument.
Compare the arguments or main ideas of two sources.
Explain how claims or evidence support, modify, or refute a source's argument.
Identify and describe a historical context for a specific historical development or process.
Explain how a specific historical development or process is situated within a broader historical context.
Identify patterns among or connections between historical developments and processes.
Explain how a historical development or process relates to another historical development or process.
Support an argument using specific and relevant evidence.
Use historical reasoning to explain relationships among pieces of historical evidence.
Corroborate, qualify, or modify an argument using diverse and alternative evidence in order to develop a complex argument.
